questions.question:
There are four underlined words in the sentence given below. One of them is misspelt. Choose the option with the misspelt word.
The country pledged to cut emmissions, adopt renewable energy, and fulfil its international obligations under the climate accord.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**emissions**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The word **emmissions** used in the sentence is misspelt. The correct spelling is **emissions**, which is spelled with a single **m** and a double **s**.

• The term is derived from the **Latin** word **emissio**, which stems from **emittere**, meaning to **send out** or **release**.

• In environmental and scientific contexts, **emissions** refer to the discharge of substances like **pollutants** or **greenhouse gases** (such as **CO₂** and **N₂O**) into the **atmosphere**.

• This term is a cornerstone of global climate policy, appearing frequently in documents like the **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)** and the **IPCC Assessment Reports** to quantify **carbon footprints**.

• Common usage includes phrases such as **zero-emissions vehicles** or **carbon emissions trading**, where the spelling must remain consistent with its **etymological** roots.

 **Additional Information__**

• Breakdown of correctly spelled conceptual terms:

• **Renewable**:

• Refers to energy derived from natural processes that are replenished constantly, such as **solar**, **wind**, **tidal**, and **geothermal** power.

• It is the opposite of **finite resources** like **fossil fuels** (coal, oil, and gas).

• **International**:

• Defined as something existing, occurring, or carried on between two or more **nations**.

• It often modifies nouns like **law**, **trade**, or **agreements** to denote **global cooperation**.

• **Obligations**:

• In a legal context, these are requirements or **duties** imposed by **contracts**, **treaties**, or **statutes**.

• Under the **climate accord** mentioned, countries have **binding** or **non-binding** obligations to reduce their **environmental impact**.

</ul

questions.question: Choose the word that is most opposite in meaning to "consistent".

• **Example: **The athlete's **consistent** training schedule allowed him to break the world record.

• **Example: **The electricity supply was **erratic** during the storm, causing the lights to flicker constantly.

She informed her teacher, who appreciated her and asked the class to make a "Save Electricity" chart. The class then decided to turn off switches before leaving any room. • The teacher's reaction to create a **'Save Electricity'** chart further confirms that the observation was related to **electricity being wasted**.

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
The company will release the new product next week.

options.text: The new product will be released by the company next week.
The new product is going to release by the company next week.
The new product will have been released by the company next week.
The new product was released by the company next week.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The new product will be released by the company next week**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The given sentence is in the **Active Voice** and the **Simple Future Tense**. The structure of the active sentence is: **Subject (The company) + will + V1 (release) + Object (the new product) + Time Reference (next week)**.

• To convert a sentence from active to passive voice in the **Simple Future Tense**, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence. The auxiliary verb **will** is followed by **be** and the **Past Participle (V3)** form of the main verb.

• The **Past Participle** of the verb **release** is **released**. Thus, the construction becomes: **The new product + will + be + released**.

• In the passive voice, the **agent** (the original subject) is usually introduced by the preposition **by**. Therefore, **by the company** is added after the verb phrase.

• Combining these elements, the correct passive structure is: **The new product will be released by the company next week**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Voice Transformation Rules**:

• **Future Perfect Tense**: If the active sentence was in the **Future Perfect** (e.g., will have released), the passive form would use **will have been released**. This is why option 3 is incorrect for the given sentence.

• **Simple Past Tense**: The passive structure **was released** is reserved for the **Simple Past Tense** (e.g., The company released the product). Since the original sentence uses **will**, option 4 is grammatically mismatched in terms of tense.

• **Going to form**: While **is going to** indicates future intent, the phrasing **is going to release** in option 2 is still in the active voice and lacks the **be + V3** structure required for a passive construction.

• **Subject-Object Swap**: The primary function of the passive voice is to shift the **focus** from the performer of the action (The company) to the receiver of the action (The new product).

</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
Have you ever tasted traditional Japanese tea?

options.text: Has traditional Japanese tea ever been tasted by you?
Was traditional Japanese tea ever tasted by you?
Is traditional Japanese tea ever tasted by you?
Will traditional Japanese tea ever be tasted by you?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Has traditional Japanese tea ever been tasted by you?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The provided sentence is an **interrogative sentence** in the **Present Perfect Tense**, which describes an action that happened at an unspecified time before now. The active structure follows: **Have/Has + Subject + ever + Past Participle (V3) + Object?**

• In the process of **Passive Voice** conversion, the **Object** of the active sentence (**traditional Japanese tea**) transitions to the **Subject** position.

• Because **traditional Japanese tea** is a **singular uncountable noun**, the auxiliary verb **Have** is replaced by **Has** to ensure proper **Subject-Verb Agreement**.

• The formula for the **Passive Voice** in the **Present Perfect** interrogative form is: **Has/Have + New Subject + ever + been + V3 + by + Agent?**

• The word **been** is the mandatory auxiliary used in all perfect passive constructions to indicate the passive state of the perfect tense.

• The **agent**, which is the original subject **you**, is placed at the end of the sentence following the preposition **by**, maintaining the question format.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Analysis of Incorrect Tenses**:

• **Simple Past (Option 2)**: Uses the auxiliary **Was**. This is incorrect because the **Simple Past** passive refers to a specific completed point in time, whereas the **Present Perfect** refers to experience.

• **Simple Present (Option 3)**: Uses the auxiliary **Is**. This represents a habitual or general action rather than a completed experience or result.

• **Future Simple (Option 4)**: Uses the auxiliary **Will**. This changes the temporal context of the sentence from the past/present to the future.

• **Active vs. Passive Voice**:

• In **Active Voice**, the focus is on the **doer** of the action (**you**).

• In **Passive Voice**, the focus shifts to the **receiver** or the **experience** itself (**traditional Japanese tea**).

</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?
New security measures are being introduced by the airport authorities to ensure passenger safety.

options.text: The airport authorities introduce new security measures to ensure passenger safety.
The airport authorities introduced new security measures to ensure passenger safety.
The airport authorities are introducing new security measures to ensure passenger safety.
The airport authorities have introduced new security measures to ensure passenger safety.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The airport authorities are introducing new security measures to ensure passenger safety.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The given sentence is in the **Passive Voice** and follows the **Present Continuous Tense** structure, which is identified by the phrase **are being introduced**.

• The general rule for **Passive Voice** in the **Present Continuous** is: **Object + am/is/are + being + V3 (Past Participle) + by + Subject**.

• To convert this into the **Active Voice**, the **Agent** of the action (the airport authorities) must become the **Subject** of the sentence.

• The **Active Voice** structure for the **Present Continuous Tense** is: **Subject + am/is/are + V1 + ing (Present Participle) + Object**.

• Applying this rule, **are being introduced** is transformed into the active form **are introducing** to maintain the continuous nature of the action.

• The original subject **New security measures** shifts to the **Object** position, following the main verb.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• Understanding **Tense Consistency** in Voice Conversion:

• **Simple Present**: Phrases like 'the airport authorities introduce' represent habitual actions or universal truths, which would change the specific context of the original sentence.

• **Simple Past**: Using the word 'introduced' implies the action was completed in the past, failing to match the **Present Continuous** auxiliary **being**.

• **Present Perfect**: The structure 'have introduced' refers to an action that has just been completed, which differs from the ongoing action described in the passive sentence.

• **Infinitive Phrase**: The phrase **to ensure passenger safety** remains unchanged in both active and passive forms as it acts as a **prepositional phrase of purpose**.

</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?
The invention of the telescope was followed by rapid discoveries in astronomy.

options.text: Rapid discoveries in astronomy was followed by the invention of the telescope.
Rapid discoveries in astronomy follow the invention of the telescope.
Rapid discoveries in astronomy were followed by the invention of the telescope.
Rapid discoveries in astronomy followed the invention of the telescope.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rapid discoveries in astronomy followed the invention of the telescope.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence is written in the **Passive Voice** using the **Simple Past Tense** structure (Subject + was/were + V3 + by + Object).

• To convert it into the **Active Voice**, the object of the passive sentence, **rapid discoveries in astronomy**, must become the subject of the active sentence.

• The original subject, **the invention of the telescope**, moves to the position of the object in the active construction.

• The verb phrase **was followed** indicates a **Past Indefinite** action; therefore, in the active voice, the auxiliary verb **was** is removed, and the main verb is used in its second form (V2), which is **followed**.

• Combining these changes, the active sentence correctly places the **doer** at the start: **Rapid discoveries in astronomy followed the invention of the telescope.**

 **Additional Information__**

• **Active vs. Passive Voice Rules**:

• **Subject-Object Transition**: In active voice, the **subject** performs the action, whereas in passive voice, the **subject** receives the action.

• **Removal of Agent Marker**: The preposition **by** is typically used to introduce the agent in passive voice and is deleted when converting back to active voice.

• **Tense Maintenance**: The tense of the sentence must remain constant. If the passive uses **was/were + V3**, the active must use the **Simple Past (V2)**. If it used **is/am/are + V3**, the active would use the **Simple Present**.

• **Verb Forms**: Only **transitive verbs** (verbs that take an object) can typically be converted into the passive voice.

</ul

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: "No improvement required."
Unless traffic rules are not made more stringent, such terrible accidents will continue to occur.

options.text: If traffic rules are not made more stringent
Until traffic rules are not made more stringent
Till traffic rules are not made more stringent

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**If traffic rules are not made more stringent**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence contains a **double negative** error. The word **Unless** is a **subordinating conjunction** that means **if... not** or **except if**.
 
• Since **Unless** already carries a negative meaning, it should not be followed by another negative word like **not** in the same clause. Doing so creates a logical contradiction that fails to convey the intended condition.
 
• To correct this, we can either remove the word **not** (e.g., **Unless traffic rules are made...**) or replace **Unless** with **If** while keeping the negative **not**.
 
• The option **If traffic rules are not made more stringent** correctly establishes the **conditional clause**. It indicates that the failure to make rules stricter will result in the continuation of accidents.
 
• The structure **If + subject + negative verb** is a standard way to express a negative condition in English grammar, making it the most suitable replacement for the underlined part.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Understanding Conjunctions:**
 
 
• **Unless**: Used to express a **negative condition**. It is followed by an **affirmative verb**. Example: **Unless you work hard, you will not succeed**.
 
• **If... not**: This is the functional equivalent of **unless**. Example: **If you do not work hard, you will not succeed**.
 
• **Until/Till**: These are **temporal conjunctions** used to refer to a **point in time** or the duration of an action. They mean **up to the time that**. Using them in this context is incorrect because the sentence requires a **condition**, not a **time limit**.
 
• **Stringent**: This adjective means **strict**, **precise**, and **exacting**. In the context of **traffic rules**, it refers to the implementation of firm regulations to ensure safety.
 
 
</ul

P. Then he sows good quality seeds in the soil. 

Q. He waters the field regularly to help the seeds grow. 

R. The farmer removes weeds and protects the crops from insects. 

S. When the crops are ripe, he harvests them carefully. 

6. Finally, the grains are cleaned, stored, and sent to the market.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

• The passage describes the chronological process of **farming**, starting from soil preparation and ending with the sale of grains. 
• **Sentence 1** sets the stage by describing the initial step: **ploughing** the land to prepare it for **seeds**. 
• **Sentence P follows** naturally because it describes the next logical step after the land is ready: **sowing** the **good quality seeds** into the soil. 
• **Sentence Q follows P** because once the seeds are in the ground, they require **water regularly** to germinate and **grow**. 
• **Sentence R is the next step** as it describes the maintenance required during the growth phase: **removing weeds** and **protecting crops** from **insects**. 
• **Sentence S follows R** because it depicts the final stage of the field cycle: **harvesting** the crops once they are **ripe**. 
• **Sentence 6 concludes** the sequence by explaining what happens after harvest: **cleaning**, **storing**, and sending the **grains** to the **market**. 
• The correct logical sequence is **PQRS**.
